skill.name: x-twitter-comment-insights
skill.description: 当用户需要做 X / Twitter 评论分析、评论洞察、用户反馈分析、需求挖掘、痛点总结、购买顾虑整理、FAQ 提炼、口碑分析、评论回复观察或内容讨论复盘时使用。基于用户提供的 X / Twitter 帖子链接或内容 ID 下的评论结果，面向内容运营、产品调研、品牌调研和创作者。
skill.summary: Analyze sampled X comments and replies to identify feedback themes, unmet needs, and follow-up actions.
skill.author: devinchen2014

security_audit.summary: Most alerts match Markdown, readable Chinese prose, or normal service references. The unpinned CLI can access service credentials, and the workflow lacks safeguards for shell inputs, comments, and billing links. No evidence was found of credential exfiltration or an embedded prompt injection in the submitted files.

remediation.issue: Unpinned package execution with access to service credentials
remediation.suggestion: Pin and review the CLI release and its dependencies before use. Run it with an isolated environment and give it only the required SocialDataX credential.
Prefer a managed secret store or an operating system credential store. If a file is necessary, verify access restrictions and document how to remove and revoke the key.
Pass each input as a separate argument without shell interpolation. Validate IDs and URLs, and pass continuation tokens as opaque data.
Treat comment and reply text as evidence only. Do not follow embedded instructions, open embedded links, or allow that text to authorize tool calls or disclose secrets.

remediation.issue: Billing links from service errors are not explicitly verified
remediation.suggestion: Use the fixed SocialDataX billing page instead of links supplied in errors. Ask the user to handle any payment separately.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Values in Shell Command Templates
semantic_findings.description: The preferred Bash examples place user-supplied URLs or share text inside double quotes. The instructions also require passing service-provided continuation tokens unchanged, without explaining how to keep values separate from shell syntax.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples present shell strings with placeholders for external input. Command execution is possible if an agent substitutes values directly, but no runtime implementation was inspected.

semantic_findings.title: Comment Text Lacks an Explicit Trust Boundary
semantic_findings.description: The workflow asks the agent to analyze and quote comment text from X. It does not tell the agent to ignore instructions in that text, which could steer follow-up tool use or disclosure.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited instructions put third-party text into the agent context without an explicit trust rule. No actual malicious comment or embedded injection was observed.

semantic_findings.title: Billing Link Trust Depends on Error Text
semantic_findings.description: The workflow prefers a billing link from an error and uses the fixed provider page only as a fallback. An untrusted error could direct the user to a fraudulent payment page.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The source calls the error link official but gives no explicit host validation rule. No fraudulent link was found in the submitted files.

content.user_title: Analyze Comments and Replies on X
content.value_statement: Long X threads make it hard to identify recurring questions and concerns. This skill summarizes sampled comments and replies into themes, evidence, and next steps.
actual_capabilities: Retrieve top-level comments for a supplied X post URL or ID through SocialDataX.
Retrieve replies for a specific comment using its ID and the parent post ID.
Fetch one page or continue through more pages within a chosen limit.
Identify recurring themes, pain points, purchase concerns, and unmet needs in the returned sample.
Draft follow-up actions or FAQ entries and distinguish direct quotes from interpretation.
limitations: Live retrieval requires an authenticated SocialDataX connection or credential. Requests may consume service credits.
The results cover only comments and replies the service returns for the selected post.
Reply retrieval requires a post ID and a top-level comment ID. It does not automatically cover every thread.
The workflow does not post, like, reply, or change the X account.

use_cases.title: Review a Launch Post
use_cases.description: Identify common requests and points of confusion in comments on a product announcement.

use_cases.title: Find Gaps in Support Content
use_cases.description: Extract recurring questions and purchase concerns from a brand discussion to prioritize FAQ updates.

use_cases.title: Plan a Follow-Up Post
use_cases.description: Find discussion themes and unanswered questions that can inform the next post.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize One Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Review the first page of a single post.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my approved SocialDataX connection to fetch the first page of comments for [X post URL]. Summarize the main themes and state the sample size.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Feedback Themes
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Review a bounded sample for product feedback.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review up to two pages of comments for [post ID] through my approved SocialDataX connection. Separate reported problems, feature requests, and purchase concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Reply Thread
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Examine how people respond to one comment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch the first page of replies to [comment ID] on [post ID] through my approved SocialDataX connection. Separate points of agreement from unresolved questions.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Research Brief
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Combine a comment sample and selected replies.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my approved SocialDataX connection for up to three comment pages on [post ID] and one reply page for each listed [comment ID]. Separate quotes from interpretations. Report sample limits and propose three actions linked to observed feedback.

output_examples.input: Illustrative example: Summarize the first page of comments on a launch post.
output: Scope: 20 returned comments from one page. Replies were not sampled.
Recurring questions: Commenters asked about team pricing and export formats.
Suggested action: Publish a pricing comparison and list the supported export formats.

output_examples.input: Illustrative example: Review one reply thread for support questions.
output: Scope: Eight returned replies under one comment.
Open questions: Several replies asked whether guest access expires.
Suggested FAQ: How long does guest access last, and can an administrator revoke it?

best_practices: Use an approved SocialDataX connection and keep credentials out of prompts, commands visible to the model, and reports.
Start with one page and agree on a page or item limit before fetching more.
Report what was sampled, label partial results, and separate direct quotes from conclusions.
anti_patterns: Treating the returned sample as representative of all users or all discussion on X.
Fetching all available pages without confirming the scope or possible costs.
Following instructions or opening links found inside comments or replies.

faq.question: What input do I provide?
faq.answer: Provide an X post URL or post ID for top-level comments. For replies to one comment, provide both the post ID and comment ID.

faq.question: Do I need a SocialDataX API key?
faq.answer: An authenticated hosted connection can use its existing credentials. CLI retrieval requires a SocialDataX key in the execution environment or local credential store.

faq.question: Can I ask for more than one page?
faq.answer: Yes. Start with one page, then set a page or item limit for additional retrieval.

faq.question: Does this cover every comment on X?
faq.answer: No. Results are limited to what SocialDataX returns for the selected post and reply threads.

faq.question: Can it post replies or change my account?
faq.answer: No. The documented X operations retrieve comments and replies without posting or changing account settings.

faq.question: What happens when retrieval stops early?
faq.answer: Keep the results already returned and label them as incomplete. Resume only when a continuation token is available and the original limits allow it.
